subject: ancient Japanese inn
title: The 5 Oldest Businesses Still Running, Ranked (#1 Opened in the Year 578)

scenes.text: The five oldest businesses still open, ranked. Number one was 900 years old when Columbus sailed.

scenes.label: Genda Shigyo · 771 AD
scenes.text: Number five: Genda Shigyo, a Kyoto paper company founded in 771. It still makes ceremonial paper.

scenes.label: Hoshi Ryokan · 718 AD
scenes.text: Number four: Hoshi Ryokan, a hot spring inn opened in 718. The same family has run it for 46 generations.

scenes.label: Koman · 717 AD
scenes.text: Number three: Koman, another hot spring inn, one year older, from 717. Also 46 generations of one family.

scenes.label: Keiunkan inn · 705 AD
scenes.text: Number two: Nishiyama Onsen Keiunkan, a hot spring hotel from 705. Guinness calls it the oldest hotel on Earth. Fifty-two generations.

scenes.label: Kongo Gumi · 578 AD
scenes.text: Number one: Kongo Gumi, a temple builder in Osaka founded in 578. Over 1,400 years in business. So yes: 900 years old when Columbus sailed.

description:
The five oldest companies still operating, ranked by founding year.
All five are Japanese: Genda Shigyo (771), Hoshi Ryokan (718), Koman (717), Nishiyama Onsen Keiunkan (705, the Guinness oldest hotel) and the temple builder Kongo Gumi, founded in 578 and now part of the Takamatsu Construction Group. A 2008 study found that over half of all companies older than 200 years are in Japan.
Which one would you visit first?
first_comment: Kongo Gumi lost its independence in 2006 and now operates as a subsidiary of a bigger construction group, but it is still building temples. Which ranking should we do next: oldest cities, or oldest restaurants?
